Please rest in a dark quiet room and drink plenty of fluids. Findings: Blood Pressure 120/80 mmHg, Temperature 98.6 F. Follow up in 1 week.

cases.title: Mechanical Lower Back Pain
cases.reference_summary: Patient James presented with a 4-day history of acute lower back pain following heavy lifting. Red flag screening was negative for cauda equina and radiculopathy. Physical exam demonstrated lumbar paraspinal spasm with negative straight leg raise test and intact neurological exam. Diagnosed with acute mechanical lumbar strain. Prescribed Naproxen 500 mg, muscle relaxant, active mobilization, and follow-up in 2 weeks.

bart-large-cnn (original).summary: Doctor: Hello Mr. James. What can I do for you today? Patient: Hi Doctor. I injured my lower back 4 days ago while lifting heavy furniture at home. The pain is aching and stiff, rated 7 out of 10 across my lumbar spine. Doctor: Does the pain shoot down into your legs, or do you have any numbness in your groin or loss of bowel or bladder control? Diagnosis: Acute mechanical lumbar muscle strain without radiculopathy. Prescribed: Naproxen 500 mg twice daily, Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg. Follow up if pain persists after 2 weeks.

Initiated on Escitalopram 10 mg daily, CBT referral, and sleep hygiene counseling with scheduled 3-week clinical review.

flan-t5-base-samsum.summary: Patient has been feeling overwhelmed by constant worry and restlessness for the past 6 months. He cannot sleep more than 3 hours a night, his heart races, and his chest feels tight. Doctor recommends starting Escitalopram 10 mg once daily in the morning, along with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) with our clinical psychologist. Findings: Blood Pressure 124/78 mmHg, Heart Rate 86 bpm. Follow-up in 3 weeks.

cases.title: Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis (UTI)
cases.reference_summary: Patient Emily presented with a 2-day history of dysuria, urinary frequency, and suprapubic discomfort. Urinalysis was positive for nitrites and leukocyte esterase, consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis. Systemic and pyelonephritis signs were absent. Managed with oral Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days, urinary analgesic, and hydration instructions.

cases.title: Asthma Mild Exacerbation
cases.reference_summary: Patient Daniel presented with mild-to-moderate asthma exacerbation secondary to viral upper respiratory tract infection. Reported nocturnal cough, dyspnea, and frequent Albuterol rescue use. Exam showed bilateral expiratory wheezing with peak flow at 70% of baseline and SaO2 96%. Stepped up to Fluticasone/Salmeterol maintenance plus 5-day oral Prednisone 40 mg burst and 5-day follow-up.

flan-t5-base-samsum.summary: Patient's asthma has flared up over the last 3 days after catching a cold. He has been using his blue albuterol rescue inhaler around 4 to 5 times a day, but the relief only lasts about an hour. The doctor will administer one in-clinic Albuterol nebulizer treatment now and a 5-day course of oral Prednisone 40 mg daily. Findings: Oxygen Saturation 96%, Peak Flow 340 L/min. Return to clinic in 5 days.
